messages:
james: quick sync 10m1 1 launch playbook for SDRs + webinar ops. need: two tight soundbites, bench callouts (method + caveats), and inbound routing rules. link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/PLAYS-132 (view)

tara: on benches. i'll pull p50/p95 and cost deltas across our quantized + unquantized configs. will note test harness and dataset. ETA: today EOD.

sophie: messaging ask: keep 1-line lead with econ ("predictable unit economics") and 1-line reliability line ("graceful fallbacks keep apps live"). those map to both cloud API and infra buyer concerns.

alex: add Dedicated vs Private quick callout. ops teams ask about SLA + network controls -> sounds like Private.

ben_sales: procurement repro: "What happens during traffic spikes? how do you avoid model throttling?" Need a 30s reply SDRs can use.

mona: i drafted an SDR opener + two branching responses. short, natural tone. will paste sample in doc.

james: cool. also need a 1-slide benchmark methodology blurb for the webinar: what tests we ran and the caveats (dataset, seq length distribution, client-side emulation). who owns that slide?

sophie: i'll take the benchmark slide + the two 15s soundbites. will include the minimal methodology blurb.

tara: bench preview: p50 delta vs CloudA (8k tokens, quantized) ~40ms lower; steady throughput cost ~15% better. p95 variance depends on routing policy. will include raw numbers and the harness link.

alex: routing rules for SDR ops: include sample policy that prioritizes latency for paid accounts and cost for dev tier. small yaml snippet please.

mona: copied. SDR script draft:

```text
SDR: "Hi, quick note: Redwood helps teams run LLMs with predictable costs and fewer latency surprises via runtime batching, KV caching, and smart fallback routing."
If they ask about cloud APIs: "We give you similar model access but with production-grade controls: rollbacks, region failover, and cost-aware routing."
If they ask about self-hosting: "We surface the same runtime controls without the full infra lift 1 you can pick Dedicated or Private depending on control needs."
```

ben_sales: procurement reply draft: "During spikes we auto-failover to compatible variants and cross-region replicas; Dedicated customers get SLA-backed capacity and priority routing. We instrument and surface token-level cost/latency so you can audit behavior."

james: nice. tara, can you add a small caveats section under the bench numbers: client-side jitter, seq length bias, model variant parity.

tara: yep. adding notes + raw CSV link.

sophie: webinar ops: slide order suggestion: 1) problem statement (cost + reliability), 2) benchmark highlights + methodology, 3) customer vignette (1min), 4) live playbook (SDR + routing + slides), 5) Q&A + next steps.

alex: i'll mock the routing visual. sample policy for runbook:

```yaml
routing_policy:
  - name: "paid-low-latency"
    priority: high
    prefer_regions: [us-west-2, eu-west-1]
    allow_fallback: true
  - name: "dev-cost-saver"
    priority: low
    prefer_variants: [quantized-small]
    allow_fallback: false
```

mona: i've linked the webinar slide v1 and a short cheat sheet for SDRs in the doc.

ben_sales: let's add two quick rebuttals for legal/procurement: SLA summary + data residency checklist. i'll draft.

deploy-bot: marketing-playbook updated by mona (doc link). :robot_face:

james: timeline: finalize copyedit + bench caveats today. slide owners to deliver v2 by tomorrow noon. dry run Tue 10am PT. @tara @ben_sales please attend.

tara: confirmed 

ben_sales: confirmed

james: final items before merge: 1) tone pass (mona) 2) bench raw numbers + caveats (tara) 3) SDR script + two-call play (ben_sales). if all green i'll publish to launch folder at 20:00 UTC and push to comms.

mona: doing tone pass now, will push edits in 45.

sophie: i'll prepare the registration blurb and a 2-paragraph benchmark narrative for press once slides are final.

james: thank you team. small ask: keep the playbook 1 pager max. focus on soundbites + routing rules. :rocket:
